_metadata.description: Physical principles for heterostructure interface design
_metadata.purpose: Enable LLM to reason about interface construction using first-principles understanding
_metadata.usage: Reference when building heterostructure interfaces between different materials
_metadata.source: Solid state physics and thin film growth literature

lattice_matching_principles.description: Principles for matching lattices at interfaces

strain_definition.positive_strain: Tensile: the matched film length exceeds its unstrained length.
strain_definition.negative_strain: Compressive: the matched film length is smaller than its unstrained length.
strain_definition.scope: Scalar engineering strain along one matched in-plane direction; lattice mismatch with a substrate denominator is a different convention.

strain_tolerance.description: Coherency depends on material, thickness, relaxation and dislocations; there is no universal mismatch threshold separating coherent, semicoherent and incoherent interfaces.
strain_tolerance.construction: Use the explicit task strain limit in the stated reference convention; report mismatch in both in-plane directions.

supercell_matching.principle: Search integer in-plane supercells and relative orientations within an explicit area or atom budget; compare both lengths and angles.
supercell_matching.formula: Scalar mismatch for aligned directions: |m*a1 - n*a2| / (n*a2)
supercell_matching.scope: The scalar expression applies to aligned directions only; a general oblique interface requires matching two lattice vectors. Report the search bounds and any residual strain.

coincidence_site_lattice.description: CSL theory for grain boundary/interface structure
coincidence_site_lattice.low_sigma_preferred: Lower Sigma means a larger coincidence fraction; it alone does not determine boundary energy, which also depends on the plane, chemistry and atomic structure.

domain_matching.description: Integer domains of one material match integer domains of another
domain_matching.example: 4 unit cells of A match 5 unit cells of B

interface_distance.description: Initial separation estimates; choose the relevant contacting species and geometry, then verify the requested gap and interatomic contacts.

anderson_rule.description: Conduction band offset from electron affinity difference

type_I_alignment.description: Straddling gap - both carriers confined in same material

type_II_alignment.description: Staggered gap - electrons and holes in different materials

type_III_alignment.description: Broken gap - conduction band below valence band

work_function_alignment.description: Fermi level alignment at metal-semiconductor interface

fermi_level_pinning.description: Interface states can pin Fermi level
fermi_level_pinning.effect: Barrier height becomes independent of metal work function

charge_transfer.direction: From lower to higher work function material

surface_energy.wulff_construction: Equilibrium shape minimizes total surface energy

interface_energy.description: Energy of interface relative to free surfaces

critical_thickness.description: Maximum thickness before misfit dislocations form

minimum_layers.description: Illustrative starting layer counts; obey explicit tasks and assess convergence for the material and observable.

vacuum_spacing.purpose: Illustrative vacuum for an isolated slab; periodic interfaces may have no vacuum. Follow the task boundary conditions and assess image interactions.

symmetric_vs_asymmetric.symmetric: Same termination top and bottom, no net dipole

interface_construction_steps: 1. Identify crystal structures and lattice parameters
3. Calculate lattice mismatch and find optimal supercell
4. Build individual slabs with appropriate thickness
6. Stack slabs using the requested boundary conditions and vacuum, if any
7. Check periodic contacts using the active task contract and species/bond geometry
